newsitem.title: EGYPT: UN says some Palestinians on border could die.
newsitem.headline: UN says some Palestinians on border could die.

text.p: At least seven Palestinians, including an eight-year-old girl, could die if they are not evacuated to a hospital from the camp on the Egyptian-Libyan border where they are stranded, a U.N. official said on Friday.

The cases include two pregnant women in their eighth month, one of whom lost a baby earlier this year after complications, an eight-year-old girl with heart problems, and a diabetic man who is losing his sight, said Panos Moumtzis of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR)

The seven are among two hundred living in what relief workers describe as "inhuman conditions" after Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi expelled them in an attempt to expose the what he calls the futility of the PLO-Israeli peace deal.
"Their lives are at risk and they could die at any moment. Something has to happen we can't wait. It is the moral responbility of the neighbouring governments," Moumtzis said.

He told Reuters a doctor from the World Health Organisation visited the camp with a delegation from the UNHCR to evaluate the medical conditions there, where the Palestinians have lived for the past 13 months.

"The doctor has rung the alarm," Moumtzis said. "These people are feeling fed up and forgotten by the rest of the world. The camp is unfit for humans to live in. The temperature ranges from 50 centigrade in the summer to below zero in the winter."
Moumtzis said there were about 250 people in the camp, 40 of whom were the Egyptian wives or children of Palestinian men who moved between Egypt and the camp, just inside the border with Libya.

The Palestinians are among thousands expelled by Gaddafi. Most of the deportees went on to other countries but Egypt has barred anyone from entering unless they have proof they can leave the country by another border. Israel controls the entry of people to Palestinian self-rule areas.

Moumtzis said a group of about 21 university students had joined the camp in September when they were turned back by Libyan officials as they tried to return to their colleges in Libya after summer holidays.
